children: Saudi Arabia commissioned 13 renewable energy and battery energy storage system (BESS) projects with a combined capacity of 10.5 gigawatts (GW) in 2026, the Ministry of Energy in an Arabic language social media post.
The additions have increased the total capacity of renewable energy and storage projects connected to the national grid to 24.8GW, the post said.
The projects commissioned during the year comprise 7GW of solar and wind capacity and 3.5GW/14GWh of BESS.
Four solar projects account for 5.9GW of the new capacity: Haden and Al-Muwayh at 2GW each, Al-Khushaybi at 1.5GW and Tabarjal at 400MW.
The wind projects comprise the 600MW Al-Ghat development and the 500MW Waad Al Shamal project, taking newly commissioned wind capacity to 1.1GW.
Seven 500MW/2,000MWh battery storage projects were commissioned in Riyadh, Rabigh, Al-Jouf, Al-Quwayiyah, Qaisumah, Najran and Hail.
Together, the projects provide 3.5GW of power capacity and 14GWh of storage capacity, equivalent to four hours of storage at rated output.
(Writing by Majda Muhsen; Editing by Anoop Menon)

title: Saudi Arabia commissions 10.5GW of renewable energy, battery storage capacity in 2026
